preamble: Almost all the B's have the same significance.

clue.text: Part of plant of use as foodstuff

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that a portion of some useful plant can be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean curd made from soya is eaten as a protein food, so it is literally a foodstuff.

clue.text: B-British snake on straight line (following Cannon and Ball)

parts.note: the adder is Britain's only venomous snake
a ley line is a supposed straight alignment across the landscape

explanation.surface: A stammering naturalist describes a British snake lying along a straight line, with a nod to a comedy double act.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble, B stands for bandleader throughout. The bracketed nod gives the first name: jazz saxophonist and bandleader Cannonball Adderley, with Cannon and Ball being a British comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian 'Cannonball' Adderley led his own jazz groups, making him one of the puzzle's bandleaders.

indicators.note: rampant means rearing up, so in this down clue the word for male climbs upward and reads backwards

parts.note: a man is a male
Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A randy man is pointed towards the comic Viz.
explanation.walkthrough: Viz is a British adult comic, but here it is the Latin abbreviation videlicet.
explanation.definitionFit: Viz abbreviates videlicet, used in writing to mean 'that is to say' before naming things specifically.

indicators.note: something cooking is being worked on or stirred up, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Delia Smith is not making a meal fit for a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a well-known British TV cook. 'cooking' shuffles DELIASNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonidas was the Spartan king who fell at Thermopylae.

clue.text: Girl regretted opening up a little

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the run is read from bottom to top
a little of the phrase means only a short run of its letters is used

explanation.surface: A girl was a bit sorry about opening up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes ETTEDO from regrETTED Opening, and 'up' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Odette is a female first name, such as the heroine of Swan Lake.

clue.text: Second B leaves capital for rugby international

indicators.note: leaves says the named letters depart from the city

parts.note: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal
here B is simply the letter, one of the few B's not meaning bandleader

explanation.surface: A second-rate player quits the capital to play rugby for his country.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the 'almost all' exceptions: B here is just the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lion is a player picked for the British and Irish Lions rugby touring side.

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Eccles was a character in the Goon Show, so a Goon

indicators.note: barking is slang for crazy, so the word mad is rearranged

explanation.surface: A stammering report of madness in the Lancashire town of Eccles.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is a Lancashire town, but here it is a character from the Goon Show, a classic BBC radio comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Benny Goodman was the clarinettist who led a famous swing band.

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within another

parts.note: demise means end
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone died in the ninth hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B's' reads as 'B is'. END goes into HR + IX.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimi Hendrix fronted his own band, the Jimi Hendrix Experience.

clue.text: B-boxer's glove insert and boot gone west

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists, which is what goes inside a boxing glove

indicators.note: gone says a letter is no longer there

parts.note: a wellington is a rubber boot

explanation.surface: A stammered list of a boxer's kit: glove padding, and a boot gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone west' looks like an idiom for lost, but it removes W from the boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington led one of the great jazz orchestras for decades.

indicators.note: to butcher something is to hack it about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for time, so three times gives three Ts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stammering butcher, lonely in triplicate, harrumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humph!' is a nod to Humphrey Lyttelton's nickname, Humph, and adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Lyttelton was a jazz trumpeter who led his own band, as well as hosting a radio comedy show.

parts.note: a bandleader whose first name pairs with Budd, as in Britten's opera hero, and whose surname pairs with bud, as in an ear-cleaning stick

explanation.walkthrough: Billy Budd is Britten's opera of Melville's novel; a cotton bud is a cotton-tipped stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Cotton was a British dance-band leader and a radio and TV star.

definitions.meaning: a bandleader, as the preamble says
a leader of the Conservatives, whose colour is blue; 19 is LEADER

explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath the Tory prime minister shared his name with a big-band leader. Blues are British Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Two men with one name: one led a big band, the other led the Conservative Party.

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word reads the same whether read upward or downward

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone's view keeps rising and falling.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief someone holds.

clue.text: What 17 across might say is child's play?

definitions.meaning: a spy like James Bond might announce his trade in two words
a guessing game for children based on things seen

explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is BOND, the fictional British spy.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's guessing game is named for the words a spy might say of himself.

clue.text: Helps a B with order of set

parts.note: here B is simply the letter

indicators.note: an order of the letters means they are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone helps by putting a set in alphabetical order.
explanation.walkthrough: Another 'almost all' exception: B is just the letter. 'order of' turns SET into ETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Man crazy about a girl from Boston, say

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other
crazy means the word Man is jumbled

parts.note: Erica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man is crazy about a girl from Boston.
explanation.definitionFit: Boston is a US city, so someone from there is an example of a US citizen.

clue.text: Tie I dropped by the beach

indicators.note: dropped means the named letter is left off

parts.note: Bondi is the famous Sydney beach

explanation.surface: A tie gets dropped beside the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is something that ties or binds things together.

parts.note: blue means smutty or obscene
a bell is something that clangs

explanation.surface: A rude, embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer and clanger both suggest a blunder, but here the bloomer is a flower and the clanger is a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that flowers can be called a bloomer, and this woodland one has blue flowers.

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld
bent means inclined, as in having a bent for something

explanation.surface: Is someone unwilling, or fixed on it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disinclined' looks like one word meaning unwilling, which is the opposite of the answer; it splits into Dis and inclined.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on something at any cost means being utterly resolved.

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A stammered complaint that a cut of meat on the bone has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles BONEACUTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Basie led one of the most famous swing big bands.

clue.text: Item burnt once with a little zest, then crushed until it can be used in muesli

definitions.text: it can be used in muesli

parts.note: bras were reputedly burnt by feminist protesters

indicators.note: a little of the word is just its first letter
crushed means broken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A recipe for a burnt item with a little zest, crushed for a breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' turns UNTIL into ILNUT.
explanation.definitionFit: This large nut is one of the ingredients in some mixed breakfast cereals.

clue.text: The definitive B is a wicked thing going topless, bared bust stuck out

indicators.note: stuck says one piece is wedged inside another
bust means broken, so the letters are rearranged
going topless means losing the first letter

parts.note: a candle has a wick

explanation.surface: A risque scene where a wicked thing goes topless and bares a bust.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names B itself, the theme word, and the surface's risque picture hides a candle and a broken word.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's B stands for a person who conducts a band, so the definitive B names that role.

parts.note: here the second B is simply the letter
ilk means a type or kind

explanation.surface: A bed and breakfast of a certain kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Acker Bilk was a British clarinettist and bandleader.
explanation.definitionFit: Acker Bilk led his own jazz band, the Paramount Jazz Band.

definitions.meaning: a bandleader, as the preamble says
the final position in a ranking

explanation.walkthrough: 'B's' reads as 'B is'. James Last was a German bandleader.
explanation.definitionFit: James Last was a bandleader, and finishing at the bottom means coming in final position.

indicators.note: sadly means things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: read literally, 10's sounds like tens, ignoring the cross-reference

explanation.surface: Someone scorns the era of Ellington's music.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 points to ELLINGTON, but the letters come from tens.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn or deride someone is to treat them with disdain.

parts.note: said aloud, blogs sounds like Bloggs, as in Joe Bloggs, the British name for an ordinary person
a bereavement is a loss

explanation.surface: Stammering bloggers write about a death.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Bloggs is the British everyman name, like John Doe.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Loss led a famous British dance-band orchestra.
